title: row22
live_proof: measured 2026-10-16. fts5ExprNearIsMatch points a lookahead reader at each phrase's poslist buffer (fts5LookaheadReaderInit(pPoslist->p, ...)) and rewrites that same buffer through a writer while reading it. The code's own comment argues the rewrite is safe because the new poslist is a subset of the old, so nothing unread is overwritten -- and says nothing about REALLOCATION. sqlite3Fts5PoslistWriterAppend begins with fts5BufferGrow(&rc, pBuf, 5+5+5), which calls sqlite3Fts5BufferSize and sqlite3_realloc as soon as n+15 > nSpace, so the buffer moves and the reader keeps reading the old one. Host ASan: heap-use-after-free, 52 bytes inside a freed 64-byte region, read in sqlite3Fts5PoslistNext64 (sqlite3.c:189645) <- fts5LookaheadReaderNext <- fts5ExprNearIsMatch <- fts5ExprNearTest <- fts5ExprNodeTest_STRING, freed by realloc <- sqlite3MemRealloc <- sqlite3_realloc <- sqlite3Fts5BufferSize <- sqlite3Fts5PoslistWriterAppend. Fixed upstream in 3.53.3. Note that the earlier record's description of the fix -- that upstream replaces the WriterAppend call with sqlite3Fts5PoslistSafeAppend -- does not match this pin, where WriterAppend already IS a grow followed by SafeAppend; the defect is the grow, not the append
object: the poslist buffer a lookahead reader is positioned in
lifetime_ender: WriterAppend rewrites the same buffer in place and the append reallocates it
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator: a NEAR query that drives fts5ExprNearIsMatch. The trigger has to make an append reallocate, and nSpace doubles from 64 while the retained poslist is a subset of the original, so n_new <= n_old <= nSpace and the realloc fires only when the retained length lands in the top 15 bytes of a bucket. Measured by sweeping one row of "aa bb" repeats under host ASan: silent at 50, 100, 150, 200, 400 and 500 repeats, reports at 55, 60, 118, 125, 245, 250, 255 and 505 -- the windows (49,64], (113,128], (241,256] and (497,512]. The case therefore indexes four rows, one per window, so it does not depend on the exact encoded length. Built in the fts5 group

note: TRIGGER REPLACED 2026-10-16. The 2026-10-11 note had the open question exactly right -- the in-place rewrite does run under live lookahead readers, but whether any append grows the buffer past its allocation was not established -- and the answer is that the recorded trigger never could: two rows of ten-odd words give a poslist of a few bytes against nSpace 64, so n+15 never exceeded it. The replacement indexes four rows of repeated "aa bb" whose poslists land in four different allocation buckets. Probe site 49 marks the reader init, the grow (old pointer, new pointer, n, nSpace, requested) and the read: on native memsys5 there are 8 reader inits, 46 grows, 8 of which move a buffer a reader was initialised on, and 68 reads from a moved-away buffer -- all 68 witnessed as kind=UAF off=52 n=1 req=64. The first one is the grow with n=50 nSpace=64 want=65, which is the n+15 > nSpace condition verbatim. Identical on virtual Capstone with lookaside off and on CheriBSD purecap (68 witnesses, same offset and size), and on CheriBSD the witness also prints tag=1 cb=<arena>+262144, the direct measurement of why that arm is silent. Unlike cases 05, 06 and 09 the block is not reissued before the read, so here the address judgement gets both the fact and the kind right
